rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_API_Loading {
    meta:
        description = "Detects CobaltStrike Beacon via dynamic loading of critical Windows APIs using GetProcAddress"
        author = "SOC Malware Team"
        date = "2026-04-09"
        hash = "a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $s1 = "kernel32" ascii nocase
        $s2 = "advapi32" ascii nocase
        $s3 = "user32" ascii nocase
        $s4 = "ws2_32" ascii nocase
        $s5 = "GetProcAddress" ascii nocase
        $s6 = { 8B ?? 24 ?? 33 C0 89 ?? ?? ?? 89 ?? ?? ?? 89 ?? ?? ?? } // Common API hash loop pattern
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and 
        ( $s1 and $s2 and $s3 and $s4 and $s5 and $s6 ) and 
        #s5 > 5
}

arguments.summary: DNS tunneling-based data exfiltration was detected from Engineering workstation WS-ENG-022 (10.0.12.22) belonging to user d.chen. Over a 23-minute period, 542 DNS TXT queries per minute were observed to the domain updates.cdn-telemetry.net, exhibiting high-entropy subdomain labels indicative of encoded payloads. Approximately 2.5 MB of data was exfiltrated at an estimated rate of 15 kbps. Initial investigation found no malicious processes or files on the host; however, historical logs suggest potential use of living-off-the-land binaries. The tunneling domain has been previously observed in low-severity scan events but was not flagged as malicious until now.
